problem: Embodied navigation models must aggregate information over long horizons with sparse rewards, but transformers scale quadratically with length. Prior world-model / frame-prediction work conditions on camera pose and a few buffer frames, so it misses agent dynamics and long-term memory.
motivation: A self-supervised, reward-free pretraining objective that captures navigability and environment structure could yield sample-efficient, task-general representations. Action-conditioned future-frame prediction over long trajectories forces the model to remember and synthesize views of the whole environment.
key_idea: Cast navigation as long-sequence token prediction: a spatio-temporal transformer trained on expert trajectories jointly predicts VQ-GAN tokens of the next frame (conditioned on action), the agent pose, and the next action.
insight: Ablations show the frame-prediction loss is the key ingredient: without it ObjectNav success drops from 0.35 to 0.21, and without Hindsight Trajectory Superposition to 0.28. Pose loss has negligible effect. Decision Transformer (embedding-space prediction) performs like the no-frame-prediction variant, and success rises with model size (10M/50M/100M: 0.35/0.42/0.46). NOTE: the authors withdrew the paper because results proved highly sensitive to dataset order and training regime, so the claims are not fully supported.
method: Spatio-temporal backbone: encoder-only GPT-style transformer with 8 spatial layers (attending within a frame's 256 image + pose + action tokens) and 7 temporal layers (attending across frames at the same token position), 512-dim, with a causal mask; handles sequences up to 50 frames.

Tokenization: VQ-GAN 16x16 image tokens (vocab 16,384) as frame targets; pose discretized into 3 tokens (0.1 m bins, 3.6° bins); 7 discrete actions; goal tokens (relative offset for PointNav, category for ObjectNav).
CLIP input embeddings: CLIP embeddings of frames are fed as input, while VQ-GAN tokens are the prediction targets, because VQ-GAN tokens are not semantically separable.
Three decoder heads: separate 4-layer transformers for next-frame tokens, current pose and next action, sharing the encoder. Frame head takes the next action as input; the action head takes the goal.
Loss: sum of cross-entropies over frame, pose and action tokens; the entire future frame is masked to avoid partial-frame leakage.
Hindsight Trajectory Superposition: relabel actions/goals so every valid goal state is 'stop' for ObjectNav, plus sampled PointNav goal states, superimposing several tasks on one trajectory.
Data: 8M human Habitat-Web frames; 20M ProcTHOR frames from an omniscient planner touring all target objects per scene (10k scenes).

setting.backbone: ENTL spatio-temporal transformer (96M params, 8 spatial + 7 temporal layers + 3 decoders) with CLIP image encoder and VQ-GAN tokenizer, trained from scratch
setting.training_data: Imitation on offline trajectories: 20M ProcTHOR frames (planner) for AI2-THOR; 8M Habitat-Web human demonstration frames for Habitat; 1M frames for PointNav; no reward
setting.observation: monocular RGB only (no depth, no motion sensors)
setting.action_space: low-level discrete: MoveAhead 0.25 m, MoveBack, Rotate L/R 30°, LookUp/Down 30°, Stop
setting.simulator: AI2-THOR (ProcTHOR train, RoboTHOR eval) and Habitat (MP3D)
setting.privileged: none at test time (omniscient planner used only to generate training data)

numbers.extra: trained on 20M ProcTHOR frames; EmbCLIP baseline used 200M

numbers.extra: 1M frames, RGB only; DD-PPO Depth used 50M frames

numbers_note: Localization: mean error 0.43 m (std 0.59) on RoboTHOR and 1.12 m (std 1.52) on Habitat after 50 steps. Future-frame SSIM: 0.578 RoboTHOR, 0.361 Habitat. The appendix ablation reports ENTL w/ CLIP at 0.50/0.18 (20M frames) vs MVP 0.47/0.15, which differs from the main-table 0.46/0.16.
results: With RGB only, ENTL reaches 0.95 SR / 0.91 SPL on RoboTHOR PointNav with 1M frames, matching DD-PPO Depth (0.93/0.88, 50M frames). On RoboTHOR ObjectNav it gets 0.46 SR with 20M frames vs EmbCLIP 0.52 with 200M, and beats the Decision Transformer (0.40) and Dreamer (0.31). On Habitat ObjectNav it scores 0.17 vs 0.23 for the IL baseline.
limitations: Authors withdrew the paper: results are highly sensitive to dataset order and training regime, so the claims are not fully supported.
Still below the strongest baselines on ObjectNav (SR and SPL), with low absolute Habitat performance (SR 0.17); rollouts accumulate errors and hallucinate new objects poorly.
Trained separately per simulator and task, with offline data only (no on-policy data).
